_note: Round 12 (E): the chef across the road. Name, restaurant and personality come from the seed and the district (packages/game/src/lib/rival.ts); their weekly review score is a mirror (district, week, the player's popularity), not a sim. Posts are picked by what really happened: who won last week, and yesterday's night. Smug, never cruel.

personalities.label: The Showman
personalities.bio: Flames at the table, a cape on Fridays. Has never cooked anything quietly.

theyLead: Another week, another standing ovation at {rivalPlace}. Not literally. Mostly literally.
Reviews this week: us {them}, them over the road {you}. Encore!
youLead: Reviews don't capture SPECTACLE. You can't give a flaming pudding a star rating. Well, you can. They did. It was low.
Congratulations to the place over the road on their reviews. We'll be setting something on fire tonight, unrelated.
close: Neck and neck with {restaurant} this week. Tonight: the dessert that comes with a drum roll.
Close race on {district}. Close races need a finale. We have sparklers.
yourBadNight: Heard a few people walked out over the road last night. Here, nobody leaves before the encore.
Thoughts with the team at {restaurant} after a tough night. Anyway: tonight, juggling.
yourGoodNight: Big night over the road, apparently. Lovely for them. We did a magic trick with a soufflé.
Good night for {restaurant}, I hear. We did the flaming crêpes twice. Once on purpose.

personalities.label: The Purist
personalities.bio: Four ingredients, no sauces, strong opinions about spoons.

theyLead: Reviews this week: {them} to {you}. Restraint wins. It always does, eventually.
We removed another ingredient from the menu. The reviews went up. Think about that.
youLead: Reviews are noise. The carrot knows. (Fine, they won this week. The carrot is upset.)
Some people over the road put cheese on everything. The public, sadly, enjoys this.
close: Level with {restaurant} this week. The difference will be the salt. It is always the salt.
Neck and neck. We are not worried. We are calm. We are a single, perfect pea.
yourBadNight: Rough night over the road, I hear. Too many dishes, too many problems. Simplify.
Long queues at {restaurant} last night. We had one guest. They were very happy.
yourGoodNight: The place over the road was busy. Busy is not the same as good. (It was also good. Fine.)
Lovely night for {restaurant}. We spent ours perfecting a radish.

personalities.label: The Influencer
personalities.bio: Plates the food for the camera first and the customer second. Has a ring light in the kitchen.

theyLead: {them} average on reviews this week vs over the road's {you}. Not that we're counting. We're counting.
Reviews up again. Link in bio. Also, the food is in the restaurant.
youLead: Just a reminder that reviews aren't everything. Followers are everything.
Over the road won the week on reviews. Good for them. Our pudding has nine thousand likes.
close: Neck and neck with {restaurant}. Time for a giveaway.
Close one this week. Like and share to help us win. That's how reviews work, right?
yourBadNight: Saw the queue walking out of {restaurant} last night. We had no queue. We had content.
Rough night over the road. Our ring light is free if they want to borrow it.
yourGoodNight: {restaurant} had a big night, apparently. Did they post about it? No? Then did it happen?
Good night over the road. Our {district} story got twelve views. Different metrics.

personalities.label: The Penny-Pincher
personalities.bio: Has never paid full price for anything, including the restaurant. Proud of it.

theyLead: Better reviews than over the road, AND our chips are 40p cheaper. Do the maths.
Reviews this week: {them} to {you}. Cost us nothing. Literally nothing. We didn't buy napkins.
youLead: Good reviews are easy when you spend money on food. Anyone can do that.
They won the week. They also pay full price for butter. Who's really winning?
close: Close race with {restaurant}. We're cutting prices again. And portion sizes. Don't tell anyone.
Neck and neck on reviews. We've started reusing the menus. Just the menus.
yourBadNight: Tough night over the road, I hear. Should have been cheaper.
Walk-outs at {restaurant}. Nobody walks out of a two-for-one.
yourGoodNight: Busy night at {restaurant}. Big takings. Big bills too, I bet.
Lovely night for them over the road. We saved four pounds on teabags.

personalities.label: The Old Pro
personalities.bio: Thirty years at the stove, twenty-nine of them complaining about young people.

theyLead: Reviews this week: {them} to {you}. Experience. You can't buy it. You can only get old.
Better reviews than the new lot again. I've got pans older than that restaurant.
youLead: Fine. The youngsters won the week. I'll be in the office, re-reading old reviews from 2003.
Over the road beat us on reviews. In my day you had to win for a whole year before anyone noticed.
close: Close this week. I've seen a hundred places like {restaurant} open. Some of them were quite good, I'll admit.
Level pegging. I'm making my gravy the long way tonight. Out of spite.
yourBadNight: Saw people leaving {restaurant} last night. Happened to me in 1997. You learn. Or you shut.
Rough night over the road. Tell them from me: get the prep done by four. Always by four.
yourGoodNight: They were busy over the road last night. Good. Somebody's got to keep me sharp.
Big night at {restaurant}. Reminds me of the old days. Before I got a bad knee.

personalities.label: The Health Nut
personalities.bio: Everything is spiralised. Has opinions about your gut.

theyLead: Reviews: {them} to {you}. Turns out people like feeling good. Who knew? We knew.
Up on the week. Our new beetroot latte is doing very well with people who've lost a bet.
youLead: They won on reviews. Comfort food is a short-term strategy. Discuss.
Congrats over the road. We're doing a cleanse to process our feelings.
close: Neck and neck with {restaurant}. We're adding chia seeds to everything. Everything.
Close week. Deep breaths. Organic ones.
yourBadNight: Rough night at {restaurant}. Have they tried oat milk? It solves most things. Not that, probably.
Queue trouble over the road, I hear. Stretch while you wait, people!
yourGoodNight: Busy night over the road. All that cheese. Our kale is quietly furious.
Big night at {restaurant}. We had a quiet one, spiralising. It's very centring.

personalities.label: The Grill Boss
personalities.bio: Fire, meat, a beard you could lose a spatula in. Calls everyone 'chief'.

theyLead: Reviews: {them}. Over the road: {you}. Fire wins, chief.
Another week ahead. The grill doesn't lie. The grill does burn the odd sausage.
youLead: Over the road won the week. Respect, chief. The grill and I are having a quiet word.
Reviews down. Turning the heat up. That's the answer to most things, here.
close: Close one with {restaurant}. Friday's going on the grill. All of it.
Neck and neck, chief. Bring your appetite and a fire extinguisher.
yourBadNight: Hear they had a rough one over the road. We've all burnt the onions, chief.
Walk-outs at {restaurant}. Should've smelled our brisket. Would've stayed.
yourGoodNight: Good night over the road, chief. Good for them. Better for us next week.
Big night at {restaurant}. Noted. Lighting the big grill.

personalities.label: The Fusion Fanatic
personalities.bio: Will put any two cuisines in one bun. Has called a sandwich 'a journey'.

theyLead: Reviews this week: {them} vs {you}. The sushi pasty is working. We're as surprised as you.
Ahead on reviews. Tonight's special: tikka ramen tacos. Please don't ask what's in the dip.
youLead: Over the road won the week with normal food. Bold. Old-fashioned, but bold.
They beat us on reviews. We've responded by inventing a curry trifle. Nobody asked us to.
close: Neck and neck. We're fusing harder. Kimchi crumble drops on {district} tonight.
Level with {restaurant}. Two cuisines? Why not five?
yourBadNight: Rough night over the road, I hear. Maybe add some miso? Miso fixes most things.
Queue walked out of {restaurant} last night. We'd have given them a bao. A fish-finger bao.
yourGoodNight: Big night at {restaurant}. Their {dish} is apparently great. We're fusing it with something.
Busy over the road last night. Inspiring. We're putting their {dish} in a dumpling.

winningLine.you: You're winning on reviews: {you} to their {them}.
winningLine.them: {rivalFirst} is winning on reviews: {them} to your {you}.
winningLine.none: No full week of reviews yet. {rivalFirst} is watching, though.

clippingItem.name: Framed clipping
clippingItem.caption: Gazette, page six: "{restaurant} beats {rivalPlace} three weeks running." Not for sale. Not even to {rivalFirst}.
